Discover Board Game Arena Rules summary For tips on how to play niagara, see Tips_niagara Contents 1 Objective 2 Game end 2.1 Tie break 3 Cards 4 River movement 5 Canoe movement 6 Stealing Objective Players paddle canoes along the Niagara river to collect gems of five different colours and bring them safely back to shore without being swept over the waterfall. Game end To win, a player must return either: 5 different coloured gems (1 of each) 4 gems of the same colour 7 gems of any colour Tie break The value of the gems. The gems closer to the waterfall have a higher value. In order the gems are: Gem Colour Value Amethyst Violet 1 Diamond Clear 2 Amber Yellow 3 Sapphire Blue 4 Ruby Pink 5 Cards Players have a set of 7 paddle cards which they play to determine the speed of their canoes and the speed of the river. All players must select the card they will play before the players then move their canoes in turn order. Once a card has been played it is not available to play again until all 7 cards have been played. River movement After all the players have moved their canoes the river moves causing all the canoes on the river to be swept downstream. The river moves the same number of places as the lowest value paddle card played plus or minus a modifier depending on the weather. At the beginning of the game the weather is set to 0 so there is no modification but each player also has a cloud card as part of their set of paddle cards that allows them to adjust the weather and hence make the river speed up or slow down. Canoe movement The number on the paddle card determines the number of spaces that the canoe moves - it costs 2 paddle points to pick up (or offload) a gem. Thus if a player chose their 5 card they could move their canoe 5 spaces *or* they could move their canoe 3 spaces and pick up a gem Or they could offload a gem and move their canoe 3 spaces. Both canoes may be moved with the same paddle card Both canoes are moved the same amount, the paddles points are not split between the canoes. When both canoes are out of the water only one can be launched in that turn. If both canoes are in the water they must both be moved using the full value of the paddle points - a player cannot chose not to move one canoe and must always use the full value of the paddle points. However if one of the canoes is out of the water a player may choose not to launch it. Canoes may only move upstream or downstream in a single turn - it is not permitted to change direction in the middle of the turn. However one canoe could move upstream and the second one downstream. Stealing Players may steal gems from other canoes, but only after moving upstream and only if they finish on the same space as the other player. And only if they have an empty canoe and hence space to load the gem. Turn order is therefore crucial for stealing. [Rating: 1/10] This is awful. I've played twice and couldn't wait for the game to end either time. The rules make no sense and are more a list of things that make sense that you can't do. The basic game without the Spirits expansion is particularly unplayable as there is no motivation to slow the river down enough for people to be able to retrieve any gems. I haven't had any fun playing this game, but I have bashed my head on the table a lot.

[Rating: 1/10] 02/20/07--Solid, light, goofy filler.  Visually nice looking, and there is strategy involved.  Too light to be SdJ, but then again, I think that we'll pretty much only see light games as SdJ from now on.  If I hadn't gotten this for a discount, I wouldn't have bought it, and might have actually been disappointed.  Fun, though, I'd gladly play it several more times in the right company.The board is a bit fiddly in terms of not always working as advertised, but after pushing a few discs across I noticed it seemed to flow better, so maybe the board needs some "working in."  EDIT:  Played again...

[Rating: 1/10] Perhaps it was just my experience with the store copy of this game, but when an entire board game is based around a single gimmick, and the gimmick does not work even remotely like it's supposed to, that's pretty terrible in my book.

[Rating: 1/10] Without a doubt one of the worst games I have played during my 15+ years in the hobby.

[Rating: 2/10] Played only on BSW.  There's a lot to admire in the design of this game, but for some reason I don't find the decisions in it very interesting.  I think the card based movement system may actually be too restrictive to make it a really good gamer's game.  I think it might be good as a slightly heavier than normal family game though.  UPDATE: Not playing Niagara at all anymore, so i'm dropping my rating to a 4.  UPDATE: Blech.  I'm basically done with this.  Aside from Diamant, I am pretty much fed up with light-middleweight games built around simultaneous action selection.

[Rating: 2/10] Played once with the westchester gaming group.  It's simple and fun, but not so deep or replayable.

[Rating: 2/10] I don't care for it. Get the river flowing at full speed with a couple players who want to keep it there and things get messy, fast. Couldn't wait for it to end.

[Rating: 2/10] Just bought it from a friend.  Played once since getting the game. It's a beer and pretzel board game.  More fun with non-gamers, With real gamers, this game has absolutely no end! Try picturing playing this game for 3 hours with no end in sight! I think this game is real torture.  Rules are rather simple and there is not a lot of decision making. This game shouldn't take 3 hours!  Second game was completely different from my first game a while back. Impression I first had was different. Rating dropped.  TRADED.

[Rating: 2/10] A játék szép és az alapötlet is jó, hogy mozgásban van a játéktér bejárható része, a folyó. Azonban sokszor úgy érzem, hogy még tesztelni és finomítani kellett volna a játékot, nem pedig kiadni - az év családi játéka díjat így szerintem nem érdemli ki.
